common_name: Charles Grimaldi Brugmansia (Large Fragrant Golden-Yellow Angel's Trumpet)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in moist, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; all parts of Brugmansia are toxic if ingested — plant away from children's play areas and wash hands after pruning.

directions: Charles Grimaldi is one of the most widely grown angel's trumpet cultivars, a hybrid selected for exceptionally large, pendulous, golden-yellow trumpet flowers and near-continuous bloom in warm climates, with intense fragrance that becomes especially heavy in the evening. It grows quickly into a large, multi-stemmed tropical shrub, blooming most heavily in spring and fall as temperatures moderate from summer extremes, though it flowers on and off through the growing season with generous water and feeding. Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, and expect large containers to need daily watering during summer heat. In zone 9a a hard freeze typically kills the top growth, but the plant often resprouts from mulched roots; container specimens can be moved to shelter before the first freeze. All parts are toxic if ingested, so handle pruning cuts with care and site the plant away from children's play areas.

common_name: Souvenir de Bonn Abutilon (Variegated Leaf Orange-Red Flowering Maple)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings after last frost into fertile, well-drained, evenly moist soil in full sun to partial shade; a 19th-century heirloom cultivar grown as much for its cream-edged variegated foliage as for its flowers.

directions: Souvenir de Bonn is a Victorian-era abutilon cultivar prized for its bold, maple-shaped leaves broadly edged in creamy white, giving the plant strong ornamental value even between flushes of bloom. Pendant, bell-shaped flowers in soft orange with darker red veining appear over a long season against the variegated foliage, and hummingbirds visit the blooms regularly. Plant in fertile, well-drained, evenly moist soil in full sun to partial shade — some afternoon shade helps preserve the leaf variegation and prevents scorch in peak summer heat. In zone 8, expect frost dieback most winters, with plants often resprouting from the base if the roots are mulched; where hard freezes are frequent, grow it in a container that can be moved to shelter for winter.

common_name: Kentish Belle Abutilon (Pendulous Apricot-and-Maroon Flowering Maple)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings after last frost into fertile, well-drained, evenly moist soil in full sun to partial shade; a classic hybrid between Abutilon megapotamicum and A. pictum, with a graceful, arching, semi-trailing habit.

directions: Kentish Belle is a long-cultivated hybrid abutilon bearing distinctive bicolor bell-shaped flowers — a dusky maroon-red calyx surrounding soft apricot-orange petals — held on slender, arching stems that give the whole plant a graceful, semi-trailing habit well suited to a hanging basket, tall container, or a spot where its wands of bloom can cascade over a wall or edge. It flowers over a long season from spring through fall and draws hummingbirds steadily throughout. Plant in fertile, well-drained, evenly moist soil in full sun to partial shade, with some afternoon shade helpful in the hottest part of a Gulf South summer. In zone 8, frost usually kills the top growth in winter, but the plant often resprouts from mulched roots; in colder areas, grow it in a container that can be sheltered over winter.
